JAIN CAVE AND LAKESIDE MONUMENTS

Cave 4 (Jainism):
Carved in the late 6th to early 7th century CE, dedicated to Jain Tirthankaras. The sanctum holds a
serene sculpture of Lord Mahavira seated on a lion throne (Simhasana). The verandah walls feature
Parshvanatha sheltered by a multi-hooded cobra and Bahubali (Gommata) standing in deep
kayotsarga meditation with creepers climbing his legs.

BHUTANATHA TEMPLE COMPLEX
Located on the eastern edge of Agastya Lake, the Bhutanatha group of sandstone temples dates from
the 7th to 11th centuries. Built in early Dravida style, its open mandapa extends directly into the
tranquil lake waters, creating one of Karnataka's most famous heritage vistas.

[2] (Source: Badami_Caves_Guide.pdf, Page 2 | Section: Cave 3 (Maha-Vishnu))
DETAILED DESCRIPTIONS OF BADAMI CAVES

Cave 1 (Shaivism):
Dedicated to Lord Shiva, carved around 550 CE. Features the iconic 18-armed dancing Nataraja relief
portraying 81 distinct mudras and postures of classical dance. Also contains monumental reliefs of
Harihara (half Shiva, half Vishnu) and Ardhanarishvara (half Shiva, half Parvati).

Cave 2 (Vaishnavism):
Dedicated to Lord Vishnu, reached by a flight of 64 steps from Cave 1. Noted for colossal ceiling
carvings and relief panels of Vishnu in his cosmic avatar Trivikrama (Vamana) with one foot planted on
Earth and another raised to the heavens, as well as the boar avatar Varaha rescuing Bhudevi.
=== EVIDENCE END ===
